thesis: Exelixis reported Q3 2026 on Oct 29 (8-K), within 15 trading days. Total revenue was $658.7M, U.S. cabozantinib franchise net product revenue was $604.9M, and non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.94. Full-year revenue guidance was held at $2.50-2.55B after the August cut. The Federal Circuit's Aug 31, 2026 ruling upheld key cabozantinib patents, and the company says MSN's generic can launch no earlier than Jan 15, 2030. Offsetting this, the zanzalintinib colorectal NDA review was reportedly extended to Mar 3, 2027, and STELLAR-304 topline results slipped to Q1 2027, a second delay. A second patent trial against MSN, on the '039 low-impurity patent, is scheduled to begin in November 2026. That scheduled trial is an active_litigation risk flag, which keeps this low even though the stock trades near its 52-week high on 2.4x volume.
invalidation: The November MSN patent trial goes against Exelixis, a further zanzalintinib regulatory or pivotal-trial delay, or cabozantinib revenue falls short of the held guidance.
sources: Exelixis IR (MSN patent appeal update): https://ir.exelixis.com/node/27706

thesis: Newell Brands reported Q3 2026 on Oct 30 (8-K), within 15 trading days, and the shares extended the post-report rally today, up about 15% to $5.97 on 3.1x volume. Net sales rose 3.7% to $1.9B (core +3.3%), the second straight quarter of growth, and normalized operating margin improved to 9.8% from 8.9%. The full-year sales outlook was reportedly raised to 2-3%. The strongest counter-case is earnings quality and earnings power, and it is not resolved. A $101M non-cash tradename impairment in the H&CS segment cut GAAP operating margin to 1.4% and produced an $81M net loss. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $0.74-0.76 was only maintained despite the Q3 beat, and part of Q2's EPS growth came from a one-time tariff recovery. UBS (Neutral, $5.75) and Citi ($5.50) set targets below today's price. Litigation: the 2023 SEC settlement now falls outside the 3-year window, and the certified baby-product class actions and Delaware derivative suit have no scheduled next step identified. The Oct 26 COO appointment is a new role, not a departure. This is medium: a confirmed catalyst with the counter-case named but not dismissed.
invalidation: Q4 results miss the $0.17-0.19 EPS guide or sales growth stalls, a further impairment in H&CS, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$5.08).

thesis: Estee Lauder reported fiscal Q1 2027 today (8-K), on 2.7x volume. Sales rose 7% to about $3.72B (organic +6%), fragrance organic sales rose 20%, and adjusted EPS of $0.72 beat the ~$0.51 consensus. The company raised its fiscal 2027 outlook: organic sales growth to 4-5.5% from 3-5%, adjusted EPS to $3.20-3.45 from $3.10-3.35, and 170-250bp of operating-margin expansion. The shares opened near $113 but reversed to close down about 3.9% at $104.99. Coverage attributes that reversal mainly to the stock having run 27.7% in three months, which is valuation and price action, not a fundamental counter-case. The fundamental counter-cases are named but not resolved: a one-time gift-card tailwind flagged by one outlet, and the macro, geopolitical and travel-retail risks management itself warned about. The $210M securities class action settlement received final court approval on Oct 14, 2026, leaving no scheduled step, and this run found no restatement. This is medium.
invalidation: Fiscal Q2 results walk back the raised outlook, or travel-retail or China weakness reverses the organic sales acceleration, or a close below the pre-report level (~$109.23) persists alongside a fundamental negative.

thesis: Tempus AI reported Q3 2026 today before the open (8-K), and the stock rose about 8.7% to $78.47 on 2.6x volume. Revenue rose 23% to $411.5M and adjusted EBITDA reached $25.6M, against $1.5M a year earlier. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $1.60-1.605B, with about $65M of adjusted EBITDA. New multi-year data agreements with Bristol Myers Squibb and Pathos are expected to add about $192.5M of data and applications revenue over about five years. The strongest counter-case is revenue quality, and it is not resolved. The pending 2025 securities class action (Shouse v. Tempus AI, N.D. Ill.) alleges inflated related-party contracts, including Pathos-linked arrangements, and today's Pathos deal is again with that related party. The company is also still GAAP-unprofitable (-$0.08 per share), and growth has slowed sharply from 85% a year ago. The class action has no scheduled ruling identified, the 2025 short-seller report alone is not a confirmed governance event, and this run found no equity raise in the last 90 days, so no risk flags apply. This is medium.
invalidation: Related-party revenue concerns are substantiated (a ruling, restatement or disclosure), growth slows further against the raised guide, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$72.22).

thesis: Venture Global gapped down from $14.79 to open at $14.16 and closed about 13% lower at $12.87 on 2.4x volume. This run found no company-specific disclosure that explains the move. Q3 2026 results are due before the open on Nov 10, a pending binary event, and Goldman had already cut its Q3 EBITDA estimate below consensus. The legal overhang is large and unresolved. The BP arbitration damages phase, with claimed damages reported at $3.7B to more than $6B, is unscheduled but anticipated in 2026-2027, and a separate adverse award to Galp on CP1 was noted in October. With the move unexplained and the earnings print still pending, this is low; avoid.
invalidation: Q3 results on Nov 10 show stable liquefaction margins and the BP damages exposure is contained or settled.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 20). CLF closed flat at $14.27, well above the ~$12.12 pre-report level, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 19 Q3 report: adjusted EBITDA of $612M on $5.61B revenue, Q4 guided to about $715M, and 2027 guided above $4B. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open. The outlook depends on contract changes and steel-price forecasts, and the Stelco layoff dispute with Ottawa has escalated, with the CEO publicly criticizing Prime Minister Carney while the company says it is fully complying with its Stelco undertakings. A Reuters-reported US-Canada push to ease steel tariffs is a possible offset but is not yet a deal. This stays medium.
invalidation: Steel prices or contract pricing weaken enough to put the Q4/2027 EBITDA outlook at risk, a confirmed material Stelco shutdown or forced sale, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$12.12).
sources: Yahoo Finance (CLF news, Stelco dispute): https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CLF/news/

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). ROIV fell about 2.8% to $35.89, still above its ~$34.92 pre-announcement level, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 21 CLARITY Phase 3 results: brepocitinib met the primary and every key secondary endpoint in non-infectious uveitis, including resolving macular edema. The drug is already FDA-approved for dermatomyositis as Lisraya. The counter-case named in the prior thesis remains open: the uveitis indication is not yet approved, and the sNDA is not planned until 1H 2027. The LNP patent litigation was settled earlier, so it is not an active legal step. Fiscal Q2 results on Nov 9 are the next scheduled event. This stays medium.
invalidation: Full CLARITY data or FDA feedback reveal a safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).
